# linux_patch (Resource)

Applies a unified diff to an existing file, and reverts it on destroy. The diff is applied by the provider, so the host does not need `patch`. Hunks must match exactly, but may have moved, as with `patch`. When the file no longer contains the change, Terraform plans to apply it again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_patch" "sshd_root_login" {
  path  = "/etc/ssh/sshd_config"
  patch = <<-EOT
    --- a/etc/ssh/sshd_config
    +++ b/etc/ssh/sshd_config
    @@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
     Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf
    -#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password
    +PermitRootLogin no
     #StrictModes yes
  EOT
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `patch` (String) Unified diff (`diff -u`, `git diff`) touching a single file.
- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file to patch. File names in the diff headers are ignored.

### Optional

- `revert_on_destroy` (Boolean) Revert the patch when the resource is destroyed. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Path of the file and digest of the diff.
